subject: Post-call: Prompt cost strategy, batching & ops next steps
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Lim <sarah.lim@moneystream.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 14 May 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Prompt cost strategy, batching & ops next steps

Sarah — thanks again for the time earlier. Short recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment. I focused this on the cost levers we discussed (token economics, batching/caching, and ops constraints).

Key pain points you emphasized:
- High per-transaction cost at scale (customer-facing prompts that hit 1M+ monthly requests)
- Latency SLAs for checkout flow: 95th p95 < 350ms is a hard requirement
- Limited infra ops bandwidth to manage multiple model variants or complex quant pipelines

Goals from our call:
1) Prove unit economics at 50% of your target token budget for a 3-month pilot
2) Keep avg latency under 300ms p95 for N=95% of traffic during pilot windows
3) Define a low-touch ops path (Redwood-managed batching + KV prefix cache) so your infra team isn’t overloaded

Proposed pilot (high level):
- 6-week pilot with a single Redwood Dedicated pool (reserved burst) running a quantized model variant for the checkout prompt set
- Workload configuration: continuous micro-batching with dynamic batch cap tuned to 70ms queuing target; prefix KV cache for common user intents (we’ll pre-populate top ~20% of prefixes)
- Measurement: tokens/response, avg latency, p95 latency, cache hit rate, and cost-per-converted-transaction (we’ll use your provided conversion uplift metrics)

ROI framing (initial back-of-envelope using the numbers you gave):
- Current cost: ~$0.015/token (your present provider) with avg request = 120 tokens => $0.0018/request
- Redwood expected (with quantized variant + batching): ~$0.004/token equivalent = $0.00048/request (assuming 3x token reduction effect from batching & cache)
- If 1M monthly requests, estimated monthly savings: ~$1,320 (conservative). If conversion uplift >= 0.15%, economics look 3–6x favorable over pilot period. We’ll run a sensitivity table once we get exact volumes.

Attachments: pilot-scope.pdf (outline + measurement plan) and sample-token-modeling.csv (simple sensitivity model).

Immediate asks / next steps:
- Can you share a sanitized sample of 2k checkout prompts and an approximate QPS distribution by Tuesday (5/18)?
- Can Tom confirm budget gate for a $15k pilot spend cap (this will cover Dedicated pool + observability retention)?
- I’ll put together a one-page mutual action plan and an ops playbook for the pilot by Monday.

If that matches what you took away, I’ll loop in Solutions Engineering to schedule the pilot kickoff next week.

Thanks,
Diego Fernandez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
D: +1 415-555-0182

- The 1M monthly requests number is across three customer flows; the checkout flow is ~420k/mo (most important for latency)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: diego.fernandez@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 15 May 2026 09:42:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Post-call: Prompt cost strategy, batching & ops next steps

Quick internal note — forwarding for ops/questions. Key ops items I think we should prepare before kickoff:
- Default batch policy: micro-batch window 20ms, max batch size 64, dynamic backpressure at 70ms target queuing. Recommend starting with those and tune after first day.
- KV cache pre-population: ask Sarah for top 500 prefixes and top intents; we’ll seed cache and measure hit-rate target >= 35% for 1st two weeks.
- Fallback plan: if p95 exceeds 350ms for more than 10% of windows, auto-fallback to smaller model variant with Canary routing for 10 minutes and notify the team.

Ben — can you prepare an initial cost sensitivity table (tokens per request buckets: 80/120/200) and projected monthly spend under the $15k cap? Attach to MAP draft.

Marissa
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
